question: How does a cyclone separator separate fine and coarse particles in a liquid stream?
expected_answer: Centrifugal force separates particles. Coarser particles move towards the cyclone wall and exit through the underflow, while finer particles generally leave through the overflow.

question: What is the primary purpose of a dewatering cyclone, and which output is considered the desired product?
expected_answer: It separates most of the water from coarse solids. The underflow, containing concentrated solids, is the desired product.
system_answer: A cyclone always operates with a size classification mechanism, but depending on the way a cyclone is used, it can be named differently: Dewatering Cyclone: If the feed is fairly coarse, the cyclone will split almost all of the water, with very little solids to the overflow. Slimes Dam Building: This is a variant of the dewatering cyclone, where the underflow is used to build the tailings dam wall. [sect7a.pdf p.1], [sect7a.pdf p.1]

question: What are the common operational problems experienced by gas cyclones and multiclones?
expected_answer: Erosion, plugging of the dust outlet or gas inlet vanes, corrosion from acid gases, and air inleakage.
system_answer: Common operational problems experienced with cyclones and multiclones include erosion of cyclone components that come into contact with high velocity particles; plugging of the dust outlet or the gas inlet vanes; corrosion from contact with acid gases in the inlet gas stream; and air inleakage that affects the inlet velocity and control efficiency of the cyclone. Multiclones are sized to include the minimum number of tubes needed to treat the required gas volume without exceeding the maximum flow per tube. [B_12a.pdf p.1], [B_12a.pdf p.1]
